title: SAP Sales Interface Catalog
purpose: Map sales business steps to practical integration contracts: IDoc or EDI messages, object APIs, web services, and business events.
decision_rule: Start with the business document, direction, latency and partner. Choose the technology after the contract is clear.
memory_rules: IDoc or B2B message moves a business document between partners or systems.
An API reads or changes the current business object when a caller needs a direct contract.
A business event says that something happened. It is not the complete business document.
Use an event plus an API read when consumers need loose coupling but also need current object details.

processes.title: Sales order intake

contracts.name: ORDERS / ORDERS05
contracts.best_for: Stable B2B order intake from customers, EDI gateways or partner networks.
contracts.configuration: Partner profile, port, inbound message/process code and partner mapping. In classic SD EDI, the external buyer document is converted into an IDoc before application posting.

contracts.name: Sales Order (A2X)
contracts.mode: Synchronous; V4 also supports asynchronous processing for supported operations
contracts.best_for: Apps, commerce or side-by-side services that need a direct sales-order contract.
contracts.configuration: Select the released API and communication scenario. Configure communication user/system/arrangement in cloud, or the corresponding service endpoint and security in private/on-premise landscapes.

contracts.name: Sales Order Bulk Request
contracts.best_for: Reliable landscape-to-landscape order creation where the sender does not wait for one UI transaction.
contracts.configuration: Configure the service/communication scenario, message identity, duplicate handling and processing response.

contracts.name: Sales Order Events
contracts.technical_name: Created · Changed · Deleted · Overall Processing Status Changed
contracts.best_for: Notifications, workflow triggers, cache/index refresh and side-by-side reactions.
contracts.configuration: Enable business event handling, bind the required topic to the event channel or broker, and make the consumer idempotent. Fetch current detail through an API when required.

processes.lead_point: For interactive checkout, price and ATP may be synchronous. Order lifecycle notifications usually should not hold the checkout transaction open.

processes.title: Order confirmation to customer

contracts.name: ORDERSP / ORDERS05
contracts.best_for: Formal B2B confirmation of accepted quantities, dates and commercial data.
contracts.configuration: Classic SD outbound EDI uses output determination/message control plus partner profile and port. Middleware can transform the SAP IDoc into EDIFACT, ANSI X12, VDA or a partner-specific format.

processes.lead_point: A Sales Order Changed event is not an order confirmation. One is a notification; the other is a business document sent to a partner.

processes.title: Outbound delivery and ASN

contracts.name: DESADV / DELVRY
contracts.best_for: Advance shipping notification to a customer or logistics partner.
contracts.configuration: Use delivery output/message control and the partner profile. The exact DELVRY basic type depends on the integration/release contract; do not hard-code a version from another landscape.

contracts.name: Outbound Delivery (A2X)
contracts.best_for: Applications that create, read or change outbound-delivery data through a released object API.
contracts.configuration: Configure the released service and security contract. Treat delivery creation/change as object integration, not as a replacement for a partner ASN.

contracts.name: Outbound Delivery Events
contracts.technical_name: Created · Changed · Deleted · Delivery Block Changed · Picking Status Changed · Packing Status Changed · Goods Issue Status Changed
contracts.best_for: Warehouse, transport, customer-experience or monitoring reactions to delivery lifecycle changes.
contracts.configuration: Subscribe only to the event needed by the consumer. Use document type/category filters where a topic covers more than one delivery use case.

processes.lead_point: ASN and Outbound Delivery API solve different contracts. ASN communicates a shipment to a partner; the API works with the SAP delivery object.

processes.title: Billing and invoice

contracts.name: INVOIC / INVOIC02
contracts.best_for: Electronic invoice exchange with customers or EDI networks.
contracts.configuration: Billing output/message control determines when the invoice is sent; partner profile and mapping determine the technical B2B route.

contracts.name: Billing Document - Read, Cancel, GetPDF
contracts.best_for: Reading billing documents, canceling supported documents and retrieving PDF content.
contracts.configuration: Use the released communication scenario and authorizations for the supported operations.

processes.lead_point: Do not present API_BILLING_DOCUMENT_SRV as an invoice-creation API. Its documented contract is read, cancel and PDF retrieval. Invoice creation follows billing due-list/reference-document logic or other dedicated interfaces.

processes.title: Customer return

contracts.name: Customer Return (A2X)
contracts.mode: V4 supports synchronous and asynchronous processing
contracts.best_for: External return portals, customer-service apps and side-by-side return initiation.
contracts.configuration: For new integrations, evaluate the V4 contract first. Confirm supported return type and operation before assuming feature parity with GUI processing.

contracts.name: Customer Return replication / confirmation
contracts.best_for: System-to-system return replication and processing confirmation.
contracts.configuration: Use the released A2A service and its replication/service administration settings; the exact direction depends on replicate versus confirm processing.

contracts.name: Customer Return Events
contracts.technical_name: Created · Changed · Deleted · Item Created · Item Changed · Item Deleted
contracts.best_for: Triggering return follow-up, service workflow or visibility updates without polling.
contracts.configuration: Subscribe to header or item events according to the consumer need; keep the return number as the cross-system correlation key.

processes.lead_point: Return order, return delivery, inspection/refund and replacement are different objects and stages. One event stream should not hide those ownership boundaries.

processes.title: Sales quotation

contracts.name: QUOTES / ORDERS05
contracts.best_for: Classical EDI quotation exchange.
contracts.configuration: Use SD output determination plus partner profile and EDI mapping.

contracts.name: Sales Quotation (A2X)
contracts.best_for: CRM, CPQ or external applications that create and maintain quotations in S/4HANA.
contracts.configuration: Configure the released API and verify supported release/approval operations for the target edition.

contracts.name: Sales Quotation Events
contracts.technical_name: Created · Changed · Deleted · Overall Processing Status Changed
contracts.best_for: Quote lifecycle automation and CRM/CPQ synchronization triggers.
contracts.configuration: Use the event only as the trigger. Read the quotation through the API when the consumer needs the complete current state.

processes.lead_point: Quote ownership matters. If CPQ owns configuration and negotiation while S/4 owns executable commercial data, define exactly where price and status become authoritative.

processes.title: Credit memo request

contracts.name: Credit Memo Request (A2X)
contracts.mode: Synchronous in V2; V4 supports synchronous and asynchronous processing
contracts.best_for: Claims, customer-service or external workflow that creates and maintains credit memo requests.
contracts.configuration: Choose V2/V4 from required operations and target edition. Keep reason, reference and approval/block status visible across systems.

contracts.name: Credit Memo Request Events
contracts.technical_name: Created · Changed · Deleted · Overall Block Status Changed · item/status events
contracts.best_for: Approval, claims visibility and downstream reaction when a request changes state.
contracts.configuration: Subscribe to the smallest event set that drives a real action; avoid mirroring every status change into another database without a business need.

processes.lead_point: A credit memo request is a sales approval/request object. The later billing document and FI posting are separate steps.

processes.title: Scheduling agreement releases

contracts.name: DELINS / DELFOR01 and DELJIT / DELFOR01
contracts.best_for: Automotive/component-supplier forecast and JIT delivery schedules.
contracts.configuration: Configure EDI inbound processing for scheduling agreement releases, customer/material mapping, cumulative quantities and the relevant delivery-schedule controls. Treat this as a release stream against an agreement, not as repeated normal sales orders.

contracts.name: Sales Scheduling Agreement (A2X)
contracts.best_for: Direct application integration for scheduling-agreement headers/items and supported actions.
contracts.configuration: Use the released API for the business object. Do not assume that an object API reproduces every automotive EDI release semantic.

processes.lead_point: Forecast/JIT delivery schedules are time-phased releases against a long-lived agreement. Modeling each release as a normal order loses the automotive control model.

configuration_playbook.title: IDoc / EDI
configuration_playbook.scope: Classic ECC and S/4HANA on-premise/private patterns; cloud B2B scenarios may expose different managed contracts.
steps: Choose the business message, direction and partner contract first.
Define the technical port. WE21 is the classic port-maintenance transaction.
Maintain the partner profile and inbound/outbound parameters. WE20 is the classic partner-profile transaction.
Assign the message/basic type and process handling required by the scenario.
For SD outbound documents, configure the relevant output/message determination so the business document actually triggers the message.
Keep EDI syntax conversion and partner-specific mapping in the integration layer where possible.
monitoring: WE02 displays IDocs; BD87 is used for status-based reprocessing/monitoring in classic ALE operations.
Check the business document after technical success. A technically processed IDoc is not proof that the end-to-end business promise is correct.
Trace partner, message type, basic type, external reference and application document together.

configuration_playbook.title: OData / SOAP API
configuration_playbook.scope: Released S/4HANA integration APIs. Exact setup depends on Public Edition versus private/on-premise deployment.
steps: Choose the released business-object API and confirm supported operations for the target edition and release.
Choose synchronous or asynchronous processing from the caller's business need, not from a general preference.
Configure the communication scenario/arrangement in S/4HANA Cloud, or the corresponding service endpoint and security in private/on-premise landscapes.
Define authentication, technical user or client identity, authorization and network route.
Define external reference, correlation and idempotency rules before volume arrives.
Keep retries safe. A timeout does not prove that the business object was not created.
monitoring: Log the correlation ID, HTTP/SOAP response and created SAP document key.
Separate transport/security errors from application validation errors.
For asynchronous APIs, monitor processing results, not only HTTP acceptance.

configuration_playbook.title: Business Events / Event Mesh
configuration_playbook.scope: Event-driven extension and integration. Events notify consumers; they do not replace transactional APIs or partner documents.
steps: Choose the business event that represents a useful state transition.
For S/4HANA private/on-premise Enterprise Event Enablement, configure an Event Mesh channel; /IWXBE/CONFIG is the standard channel configuration entry point.
Create and activate the outbound binding/topic for the required business object event.
Configure the broker queue/subscription and consumer permissions.
Make consumers idempotent and define retry/dead-letter handling in the messaging layer.
If the event payload is intentionally small, use the business key to read current state through a released API.
monitoring: Monitor both producer channel health and broker queue/consumer health.
Track event ID/business key so duplicate delivery is harmless.
Do not treat event ordering across unrelated objects as a guaranteed business transaction unless the platform contract explicitly says so.

release_boundaries.rule: IDoc/EDI plus message control is a normal integration pattern. Transactions such as WE20, WE21 and WE02 belong here.
Classic IDoc patterns still coexist with released OData/SOAP APIs and Enterprise Event Enablement. Architecture is mixed by design.
Prefer released APIs, communication scenarios/arrangements, managed B2B content and released business events. Do not copy an on-premise transaction-code setup into Public Edition documentation.

lead_checks: What business document crosses the boundary?
Who is the sender and who is the system of record?
Does the caller need an immediate business answer, or only reliable later processing?
Is this a partner document, an object API call, or a notification event?
What key lets support correlate the external message, SAP object and downstream follow-up?
How are duplicate delivery, retries and partial business failures handled?
Which part changes between ECC, S/4HANA private and Public Edition?
